attribution.note: Marcus presents the prediction as his own conclusion.

semantics.note: The normalisation preserves the universal claim about competing AI builders and their eventual investment returns. Intense competition is asserted as the expected regime, rather than offered as a hypothetical antecedent.

contract.note: The contract fairly reads overpayment as investment costs unjustified by eventual attributable profits. It preserves the unspecified horizon and does not treat temporary losses or company-wide profits as decisive.

evidence.note: Timely Alphabet disclosure of quarterly consolidated cash flow. It does not establish completed AI investment returns.
Timely Microsoft management expectation of favorable returns. Neither that expectation nor consolidated financial performance establishes a realized AI investment counterexample.
Timely Anthropic filing disclosing losses and profitability risks. These do not establish eventual overpayment; reported losses also include substantial valuation-related accounting charges.

reviews.rationale: No deadline was supplied, and the packet contains no decisive event establishing completed investment economics. Current cash flows, profitability risks, and management expectations settle neither eventual inadequate returns across all competing builders nor a realized counterexample.
